value.body: Mission Vatsalya is the Ministry of Women and Child Development's child-protection scheme, which replaced the earlier ICPS. It funds District Child Protection Units (DCPUs) that implement the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 — handling children in need of care, adoption and foster care, child-care institutions, and support to Child Welfare Committees and Juvenile Justice Boards.

items.label: Typical DCPU posts
items.value: District Child Protection Officer, Protection Officer, Legal-cum-Probation Officer, Counsellor, Social Worker

items.label: Usual qualification
items.value: Graduate or PG in social work, sociology, psychology, child development or law
items.note: LLB for Legal-cum-Probation Officer; experience often required

items.label: DCPO remuneration
items.note: As notified in one state's DCPU advertisement
items.source: Nagaland DCPU notice under Mission Vatsalya (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Posts are filled by state and district authorities through their own advertisements, usually by application screening and interview. A BSW meets the requirement for some posts; senior posts typically ask for an MSW or other PG degree plus experience.

value.title: At a glance
items: Posts are contractual and scheme-funded, not permanent government jobs.
The work involves home visits, court and committee work, and difficult child-protection cases.
The experience is relevant to NGOs, UN agencies and state social welfare departments.
